name: Markwayne Mullin
role: US Senator from Oklahoma (2023–2026), US Representative (2013–2023), US Secretary of Homeland Security (from March 2026)
summary: Republican politician and Trump ally whose record is conservative on taxes, spending, regulation, guns, abortion, same-sex marriage and immigration. He voted to object to the 2020 election results in Arizona and Pennsylvania, backs tariffs and fossil fuel expansion, and has criticised but also worked with union leaders. He is a Cherokee citizen with a mixed record on tribal sovereignty.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His campaign site called Obamacare budget-busting government-run health care and favoured market-based reforms instead; he voted to repeal the ACA (2013) and for the AHCA (2017), and argues Medicaid should not broadly cover able-bodied adults.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted against the Raise the Wage Act ($15 federal minimum) in 2019 and against a 2025 Senate amendment to allow a $17 minimum; votes against specific raises, with no stated view of his own on raising it at all.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His campaign site says government does not create jobs, that the private sector is the engine of the economy and that regulation is the biggest obstacle for business; he does not compare market and state allocation as such.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Stated he opposes increasing tax rates and that "we are taxed enough"; backed the 2017 corporate rate cut.

unions-good.rationale: Criticised unions as putting leaders ahead of workers and backs right-to-work, but later described a friendly working relationship with Teamsters leader Sean O'Brien; mixed record.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Stated that excessive regulations such as EPA rules harm job growth; opposed EPA and OSHA regulations.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Signed a September 2023 letter of 14 Republican lawmakers asking the DEA to keep marijuana in Schedule I; a position on cannabis scheduling, with no recorded statement on other drugs.

limit-guns.rationale: Said the Second Amendment leaves "no wiggle room", supports assault rifle ownership; voted against universal background check bills.

empower-police-military.rationale: Voted for higher military spending and said the military should be allowed to use every tool available.

decide-locally.rationale: Backed states leasing federal-land energy rights, state marriage definitions over federal ones, and local control of education.

rehabilitation.rationale: Voted for the House FIRST STEP Act of May 2018, built around recidivism-reduction programmes in federal prisons, but against the final First Step Act in December 2018; a mixed record with no statement of his own on the aim of prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: His campaign site lists traditional values and pledges to defend traditional marriage between one man and one woman as a Christian responsibility.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Stated in 2012 that he opposes same-sex marriage; voted against the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as pro-life; cosponsored the Life at Conception Act; said in a 2022 debate he supports a federal abortion ban without exceptions.

more-religion-public.rationale: His 2024 remark was that the Bible should be taught by believers rather than by school teachers who may not be, a caution about Bible teaching in public schools, not a call for more religion in public life; no other evidence found.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His recorded positions are against amnesty and for border enforcement (unauthorised migration), and he cosponsored lifting per-country visa caps; nothing found on overall immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Original cosponsor of a 2013 resolution setting conditions on the US joining the UN Arms Trade Treaty, and voted in 2025 to take up a bill sanctioning the International Criminal Court.

free-trade.rationale: Backs tariffs and calls them balancing trade; also supported the USMCA; mixed.

open-borders.rationale: At his 2026 confirmation hearing he said DHS has "a job to secure the border" with physical barriers and technology, which rejects opening national borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Opposed EPA climate regulations and EV promotion and praised West Virginia v. EPA.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He voted for S.870, whose stated purposes include advancing nuclear energy, and championed funding for a prototype microreactor.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted for the Death Tax Repeal Act in 2015, which would abolish the federal estate tax outright.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Defended Trump tariffs: countries "got rich over the backs of the workers here in America".

political-violence-never.rationale: He disavows political violence but defends aspects of earlier fighting remarks during the same exchange; the evidence is mixed.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Cherokee citizen who in 2020 joined tribal leaders in a statement on McGirt, but later urged tribes to negotiate with Oklahoma and backed limits on one tribe's sovereignty; mixed.

school-vouchers.rationale: His campaign site says parents should be able to choose public, private or home schooling, and he voted in 2015 to reauthorise the DC private-school voucher programme (SOAR Act).

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His campaign site centres on cutting spending and the growing national debt, and he voted against the American Rescue Plan stimulus in 2021 at both House stages.

force-without-un.rationale: Defended the 2025 US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, which had no Security Council approval, as a necessary mission; he did not address UN approval as such.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted in 2013 to maintain work requirements for welfare recipients and supports workfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: He calls for partnership among business owners, workers and the administration, and for cooperation with organized labor in rebuilding domestic production.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Urged Biden to raise oil and gas production, backed Keystone XL and offshore drilling.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separated-powers.rationale: He recognises Congress’s lawmaking role but later declines unconditional compliance with judicial orders, calling courts politicised.

death-penalty.rationale: Cosponsored the Thin Blue Line Act (2016), which makes killing a police officer an aggravating factor in death-penalty cases; a cosponsorship rather than a statement of his own.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Cosponsored the EACH Act in 2013 and 2015, exempting people with sincere religious objections from the ACA insurance mandate, and his campaign site objects to forcing people of faith to violate their beliefs.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The 2012 Vote Smart survey answer that OnTheIssues reports could not be opened, and no other record of his on personal retirement accounts was found.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Voted in September 2014 for the amendment authorising the training and equipping of vetted Syrian opposition fighters, framed mainly against ISIL; one vote.

non-intervention.rationale: He endorses the strikes on Iran’s nuclear program rather than an absolute prohibition on intervention in another state.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposed 2016 guidance on transgender students and restrooms; cosponsored a bill barring transgender women from women's sports.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His active work securing military installations and new weapons funding supports retaining and strengthening the armed forces.

term-limits.rationale: Signed a 2011 campaign pledge to cosponsor and vote for congressional term limits, but U.S. Term Limits reported in 2016 that he had backed off it; a pledge his record in office did not bear out, so mixed.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He defends an officer’s lethal response to a vehicle he describes as a lethal weapon.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: His column argues that law must recognise biological differences between men and women rather than replace them with chosen gender status.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He defends the U.S. attack on Iranian nuclear facilities as accomplishing a necessary preventive mission.

future-generations.rationale: His 2014 campaign site backs "a balanced approach to protecting and preserving our nation’s natural resources for future generations" and speaks of preserving farmland for them; the qualifier "balanced" and his opposition to EPA rules keep this weak.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His defence of lawful private gun ownership and legislation protecting it directly oppose reserving arms to the army and police.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted in 2018 for a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution, the strictest form of binding fiscal rule.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Objected to Biden's student loan forgiveness plan in 2022.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Stated Oklahoma is a strong right-to-work state; recorded as backing right-to-work laws.

voter-id.rationale: He supports requiring voters to prove U.S. citizenship and identifies the SAVE America Act as constitutional.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Voted in January 2025 to take up a bill sanctioning the International Criminal Court for any effort to investigate or prosecute protected persons of the US and its allies.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Defended the 2025 lethal military strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats, asking "Why do we care if we take them out in international water?" and calling the smugglers terrorists at war with the US; he frames it as war, not as killing dealers in general.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He argues that Medicaid should concentrate on vulnerable and needy recipients rather than broadly cover able-bodied adults.

notes:
Voted Yea on objections to Arizona and Pennsylvania electors (Jan 2021) and said in 2022 it was absurd that Biden won the most votes; no matching statement exists in the list. Voted for 2022 and 2024 Ukraine aid and worked to pass the 2024 package, but no statement matches. Positions on abortion and same-sex marriage are partly from 2012 statements, confirmed by later votes. Tribal sovereignty evidence is mixed. The mullin.senate.gov site returned HTTP 403 and congress.gov was not used. Most evidence comes from secondary aggregators and Wikipedia.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 14 answers taken from it, 17 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass. Earlier audit consulted only for notes and source leads. Congressional votes are medium confidence; administrative promises are distinguished from implementation. Narrow positions on undocumented immigration do not establish a preference to reduce immigration overall. January 2021 electoral objections do not by themselves settle every statement about democracy. No attempt was made to reach the inclusion threshold. Final review left universal healthcare, low-paid-worker tax credits and general minority territorial autonomy null because the retrieved evidence concerned narrower proposals. All 490 statement texts, including the ten priority statements, were reviewed against the source set. Technology searches located military R&D and AI security issues, but no clear position on transferring government decisions to algorithms, enhancement, encryption or technological acceleration. Culture searches located personal faith and Cherokee identity, but these alone do not answer the cultural and theological propositions. Priority statements all remain null. Copy validation uses the unchanged validator in a VM with only personPath redirected to this scratchpad; no production audit was replaced.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-10-31) on line 14: added extrajudicial-killing +1 (CNN State of the Union, 30 Nov 2025, drug-boat strikes), international-criminal-courts -1 (ICC sanctions cloture vote, Jan 2025), rehabilitation 0 low (yea on the House FIRST STEP Act, nay on the final First Step Act, 2018). Re-sourced three Wikipedia-only answers: raise-minimum-wage to his 2019 and 2025 votes (lowered to -1, votes against specific raises), open-borders to the confirmation hearing, force-without-un to the June 2025 CNN interview. Searched without a usable result: Electoral College and third-term remarks (he called a third term a joke and said he would not change the Constitution unless the people choose, which does not answer unlimited re-election), trade surplus (his tariff remarks are about reciprocity, not a surplus), GM-crop labeling votes (none recorded for him), strike and picketing rules (PRO Act objections do not address strikes), precautionary principle and future generations (energy column silent).

claude-opus-5-5 OnTheIssues re-sourcing (2026-10-31): 16 answers that cited only OnTheIssues or Wikipedia were traced to originals: Voteview roll calls, GovInfo bill-status records (cosponsorships), his archived 2014 campaign issues page, and press reports. Nulled where the original could not be opened or did not settle the statement: individual-pension-accounts (2012 Vote Smart survey, HTTP 403), reduce-immigration (only unauthorised migration), more-religion-public (the Bible remark cautions against non-believer teachers). Lowered to what the original shows: markets-allocate-better +2 to +1, legalize-drugs -2 to -1, empower-international-orgs -2 to -1, death-penalty +2 to +1, term-limits +2 to 0 (pledge not borne out). Added from the same 2014 page: future-generations +1 low (a balanced approach to preserving natural resources for future generations).
